lessons.title: Listening to a story and a telephone call
lessons.objective: Listen to a short story and a telephone call, carry out tasks and answer questions.
lessons.course:
When we listen, we look for who, where, when, what and why. We can take short notes with one or two words.
On the telephone, we greet, say who is speaking, give the message clearly and repeat important information (time, place, number).
lessons.model: The adult tells a short story about a journey and then asks: “Who travelled? Where to? Why?”
lessons.guided: Listen to the call below twice. Write the time and the place of the meeting. Then answer the questions.
lessons.exercise: In a telephone call, what should we repeat?
lessons.answer: Important information like the time, the place or a number.
accept: Important information like the time, the place or a number
lessons.remediation: Listen to one sentence at a time and answer one question.
lessons.transfer: Take a short telephone message for an adult at home and write it down.

practice.prompt: Listen to the call and answer: at what time will the bus leave?
practice.listen: Hello, this is Uncle Fon. The bus to Kumba will leave the station at nine o’clock. Please be there at half past eight. Goodbye!
practice.explanation: Listen for the time after “will leave”.

practice.prompt: Where must we be at half past eight?
Which question words help us listen?
practice.explanation: These words help us find the information.

lessons.title: A picture adventure story: lost at the bus station
lessons.objective: Read a short adventure story in pictures and short texts, put oneself in the place of a character and find the lesson.
lessons.course:
An adventure story has a character, a problem, actions and an ending. In a picture story, each picture has a short text.
We imagine how the character feels and what we would do in his place.

support.title: Klassia picture story
support.text:
Picture 1: Neba and his aunt arrive at the busy bus station in Bafoussam.
Picture 2: Neba stops to watch a man selling roasted corn. His aunt walks on.
Picture 3: Neba looks around. He cannot see his aunt. He is afraid.
Picture 4: He remembers what his mother said: “If you are lost, stay where you are and ask a person in uniform.”
Picture 5: A ticket officer calls his aunt’s name on the loudspeaker. His aunt runs back and hugs him.

lessons.model: The adult reads picture 3 and asks: “How does Neba feel? What would you do?”
lessons.guided: Read the five pictures. Say the problem and the solution. Act the story in a group.
lessons.answer: He is lost at the bus station.
accept: He is lost at the bus station
lessons.remediation: Read the story with the adult picture by picture.
lessons.transfer: Discuss with your family what to do if you get lost.
lessons.materials: The picture story (text version), drawings if possible.

practice.prompt: Put the pictures in order.
items: They arrive at the bus station.
He asks a person in uniform.
practice.answer: arrive, corn seller, lost, ask, aunt comes back.

practice.prompt: What lesson does the story teach?
choices: If you are lost, stay where you are and ask a person in uniform.
Run away when you are lost.
practice.answer: If you are lost, stay where you are and ask a person in uniform.

practice.prompt: How does Neba feel in picture 3?
practice.explanation: The text says: He is afraid.

lessons.title: A narrative text: my journey
lessons.objective: Write a narrative text of about 80 words about a journey, in the right order.
lessons.course: A narrative tells a story in order: beginning (when, who, where), middle (what happened), end (how it finished, how we felt). We use the past tense and time words: one day, first, then, after that, finally.

support.title: Useful words
support.text: last holidays, bus station, ticket, luggage, road, bridge, arrived, tired, happy

lessons.model: “Last holidays, I travelled to Buea with my father. First, we bought our tickets at the station. Then the bus left at seven o’clock. On the way, I saw tea plantations and Mount Cameroon. After four hours, we arrived. My grandmother was waiting for us. I was tired but very happy.”
lessons.guided: Plan your story: beginning, middle, end. Write one sentence for each part, then add details to reach about 80 words.
lessons.exercise: Which tense do we use to tell a past journey?
lessons.remediation: Tell the story orally first, then write it.
lessons.transfer: Write about a visit to a relative.

practice.prompt: Write your journey in about 80 words.
practice.answer: A narrative with a beginning, a middle and an end, in the past tense.
practice.explanation: Use time words: first, then, after that, finally.

practice.prompt: Put the time words in a good order.
practice.explanation: Time words show the order of events.

practice.prompt: Which sentence is a good ending?
choices: I was tired but very happy.
practice.answer: I was tired but very happy.
practice.explanation: An ending says how the story finished or how we felt.

lessons.title: Prepositions of location, direction and time
lessons.objective: Use prepositions of location, direction and time in sentences.
lessons.course:
Location (where): in, on, under, beside, between, behind, in front of. The bag is under the seat.
Direction (where to): to, from, into, out of, across, along. The bus goes from Bamenda to Yaoundé. We walk across the bridge.
Time (when): at 8 o’clock, on Monday, in June, in the morning.
lessons.model: The adult describes a trip: “We left from Kumba on Monday at six o’clock. The car drove along the coast and across a bridge.”
lessons.guided: Describe a picture of a road trip using three prepositions of each kind.
lessons.exercise: The bus travels ___ Douala ___ Kribi. (from / to)
lessons.transfer: Describe the way from your house to school with prepositions.
lessons.materials: Toy car, picture of a road.

practice.prompt: Complete with at, on or in.
practice.text: We travel [[on]] Monday, [[at]] six o’clock, [[in]] the morning.
practice.answer: on Monday, at six o’clock, in the morning.
practice.explanation: on + day, at + hour, in + part of the day.

practice.prompt: Which preposition shows direction?
Match each preposition with its kind.
practice.answer: between: location; along: direction; in June: time.
practice.explanation: Prepositions show place, direction or time.

lessons.title: Telling the time: past and to
lessons.objective: Read the time on a clock face using o’clock, half past, quarter past, quarter to, past and to.
lessons.course:
The short hand shows the hours; the long hand shows the minutes. When the long hand is on 12: o’clock. On 6: half past. On 3: quarter past. On 9: quarter to.
Past: minutes after the hour (ten past seven = 7:10). To: minutes before the next hour (twenty to eight = 7:40).
lessons.model: The bus leaves at quarter past six (6:15) and arrives at half past nine (9:30).
lessons.guided: Set times on a paper clock and read them. Then read times written in figures.
lessons.exercise: The long hand is on 6 and the short hand is between 4 and 5. What time is it?
lessons.remediation: Practise o’clock and half past first.
lessons.transfer: Read the time at home when you wake up and when you go to school.
lessons.materials: A paper clock with moving hands.

practice.prompt: Match the times.
practice.explanation: Past: after the hour; to: before the next hour.

practice.prompt: How many minutes are in an hour?
Which time is “twenty to nine”?

lessons.title: Distances: metres and kilometres
lessons.objective: Use km and m to talk about distances and convert between them.
lessons.course:
Long distances are measured in kilometres: 1 km = 1 000 m. From Douala to Yaoundé is about 240 km. A football field is about 100 m long.
We add or subtract distances of a journey.
lessons.model: The adult reads road signs: “Limbe 25 km. Buea 15 km.” The bus travels 15 km, then 10 km more: 25 km.
lessons.guided: Read distances on a simple route. Add the parts of a journey.
lessons.exercise: How many metres are in 2 km?
lessons.remediation: Use 1 km = 1 000 m with whole kilometres only.
lessons.transfer: Ask an adult how far your school or the market is.
lessons.materials: A simple route drawing with distances.

practice.prompt: A bus goes 45 km, then 38 km. How many km in all?
3 km = ? m
Which unit for the distance between two towns?

lessons.title: The number line up to 30
lessons.objective: Locate and order numbers on a number line up to 30 and count in steps.
lessons.course:
A number line has equally spaced marks. We locate numbers and jump in steps: from 6, jumps of 4: 10, 14, 18…
The number line helps us add (jump right) and subtract (jump left).
lessons.model: The adult draws a line from 0 to 30 and jumps in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.
lessons.guided: Draw a number line from 0 to 30 on the ground. Place cards on it and jump in steps of 3 and 5.
lessons.exercise: Start at 12 and jump 3 steps of 4 to the right. Where do you land?
lessons.remediation: Use a line from 0 to 20 first.
lessons.transfer: Use a number line to count kilometres on a journey.

practice.prompt: Start at 27 and jump 9 to the left. Where are you?
Complete the jumps of 3.
Put the numbers in their place from left to right.
practice.explanation: Smaller numbers are on the left.

lessons.title: Problems with the four operations: the journey
lessons.objective: Choose the right operation(s) to solve problems about a journey.
lessons.course:
To solve a problem: read it, find the question, find the numbers, choose the operation, calculate, check and answer in a sentence.
+ : putting together; − : taking away or difference; × : equal groups; ÷ : sharing or grouping.
lessons.model: A taxi ticket costs 300 frs. A family of 4 travels: 4 × 300 = 1 200 frs. The adult explains each step aloud.
lessons.guided: Solve three problems. For each one, underline the question and write the operation before calculating.
lessons.exercise: A bus has 70 seats. 48 passengers are on board. How many seats are free?
lessons.remediation: Act the problem with objects before calculating.
lessons.transfer: Make up a journey problem for a friend.

practice.prompt: 5 children each pay 200 frs for a taxi. Total paid?
48 passengers share 6 taxis equally. How many in each taxi?
“How many more km?” Which operation?
practice.explanation: “How many more” asks for a difference.

lessons.title: Safety on the road and protective equipment
lessons.objective: Apply safety rules on the road and use appropriate protective equipment.
lessons.course:
On a journey, we stay safe: we wear the seat belt in a car, a helmet on a motorbike, we do not put our head or arms out of the window, we cross at safe places and look both ways.
Workers use protective equipment: helmets, gloves, boots, masks, reflective jackets.
lessons.model: Before the motorbike leaves, the driver gives Bih a helmet and checks that it is fastened.
lessons.guided: Match pictures of workers with their protective equipment. Act a safe journey by bus.
lessons.exercise: What must you wear on a motorbike?
lessons.remediation: Learn two rules first: helmet on a motorbike, seat belt in a car.
lessons.transfer: Remind your family to wear seat belts or helmets on the next trip.
lessons.materials: Pictures of road scenes and protective equipment.

practice.prompt: Match each worker with his protective equipment.
practice.answer: builder: helmet; welder: face shield; road worker: reflective jacket.

practice.prompt: Which behaviour is safe in a bus?
choices: put the head out of the window
stand near the door while moving

practice.prompt: What do we wear in a car?
practice.explanation: The seat belt protects in an accident.

lessons.title: Je vais au marché, je viens de l’école
lessons.objective: Dire où l’on va et d’où l’on vient, et indiquer un chemin (à gauche, à droite, tout droit).
lessons.course:
Pour dire où on va : « Je vais à Douala. Je vais au marché. Je vais à l’école. »
Pour dire d’où on vient : « Je viens de Yaoundé. Je viens du marché. Je viens de l’hôpital. »
Pour indiquer un chemin : à gauche, à droite, tout droit.

support.title: Dis avec l’adulte
support.text:
Je vais au marché.
Je viens de l’école.
Tourne à gauche, puis va tout droit.

lessons.model: Un voyageur demande : « Où est la gare routière ? » Bih répond : « Va tout droit, puis tourne à droite. »
lessons.guided: Dessine un petit plan de ton quartier. Explique en français le chemin de ta maison à l’école.
lessons.remediation: Travaille « à gauche » et « à droite » avec les bras.
lessons.transfer: Explique en français le chemin vers la boutique la plus proche.

practice.prompt: Complète avec au, à l’ ou à.
practice.text: Je vais [[au]] marché. Je vais [[à l’]]école. Je vais [[à]] Kribi.
practice.answer: au marché ; à l’école ; à Kribi.
practice.explanation: au + nom masculin ; à l’ + voyelle ; à + ville.

practice.prompt: « Tourne à droite » veut dire…
Écoute et suis le chemin.
practice.listen: Va tout droit. Tourne à gauche. La pharmacie est à côté de l’église.
practice.answer: Tout droit, à gauche, la pharmacie est à côté de l’église.

lessons.title: Mountains, rivers and maps
lessons.objective: Identify physical features of Cameroon and read a simple map with a key.
lessons.course:
Physical features are natural forms of the land: mountains (Mount Cameroon), hills, plains, plateaus, rivers (Sanaga, Wouri), lakes and the sea (Atlantic Ocean).
A map is a drawing of a place seen from above. It has a title, a key (symbols) and directions (North, South, East, West).
lessons.model: The adult shows a map of Cameroon: “This triangle in the key is a mountain. Mount Cameroon is near Buea.”
lessons.guided: Draw a map of your quarter with a title, a key and four directions.
lessons.exercise: What is the highest mountain in Cameroon?
lessons.remediation: Use a map with three symbols only.
lessons.transfer: Find the river nearest to your town on a map.

practice.prompt: Match each feature with an example.
practice.answer: mountain: Mount Cameroon; river: Sanaga; ocean: Atlantic.
practice.explanation: These are physical features of Cameroon.

practice.prompt: What explains the symbols of a map?
Draw a map of your quarter with a key.
practice.answer: A map with a title, a key and directions.

lessons.title: Folding and cutting: a paper boat
lessons.objective: Fold and cut paper following given dimensions to make an object.
lessons.course:
To make a good object, we follow the dimensions: we measure with a ruler, we mark with a pencil, we fold on the line and we cut carefully with scissors.
A paper boat is folded from a rectangle (for example 20 cm × 30 cm).
lessons.model: The adult measures a rectangle of 20 cm by 30 cm, cuts it and folds a boat step by step.
lessons.guided: Measure and cut a rectangle of 20 cm × 30 cm. Fold a boat following the adult. Float it on water.
lessons.exercise: Which tool do we use to measure the paper?
lessons.remediation: Fold with a ready-cut rectangle first.
lessons.transfer: Make a boat for a younger child and explain the steps.
lessons.materials: Paper, ruler, pencil, scissors (with an adult).

practice.prompt: Put the steps in order.
A rectangle of 20 cm × 30 cm. What is the longer side, in cm?
Draw your boat.
practice.answer: A drawing of the paper boat.

lessons.title: Musical instruments and the sol-fa scale
lessons.objective: Name musical instruments, keep a rhythm and sing the sol-fa scale with correct pitch.
lessons.course:
Instruments: drums and tom-toms (percussion), the balafon, the flute, the guitar, rattles. Each makes a different sound.
The sol-fa scale goes up: do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do. We sing it slowly, listening to rise in pitch, then down again.
lessons.model: The adult claps a rhythm (long, short, short) and sings the scale up and down.
lessons.guided: Repeat a clapped rhythm. Sing the sol-fa scale up and down with the adult. Make a rattle with a tin and seeds.
lessons.exercise: Which note comes after “mi” in the sol-fa scale?
lessons.remediation: Sing the first three notes: do, re, mi.
lessons.transfer: Play a rhythm on a homemade instrument for your family.
lessons.materials: A drum or a tin, seeds, a bottle.

practice.prompt: Put the notes of the scale in order.
practice.explanation: The scale goes up step by step.

practice.prompt: Which instrument do we play by hitting it?
practice.explanation: A drum is a percussion instrument.

practice.prompt: Listen and repeat the scale.
practice.listen: do, re, mi, fa, sol, la, ti, do
practice.explanation: Each note is a little higher.

lessons.title: Throwing safely: shot put and javelin with soft objects
lessons.objective: Throw a light object far using the correct movement, following safety rules.
lessons.course:
In throwing events, we throw an object as far as possible: the shot (push from the neck), the javelin (throw over the shoulder), the discus (turn and throw). At school we use soft or light objects: a bean bag, a ball, a stick of foam.
Safety: everyone stands behind the thrower; we collect the objects only when the teacher says so.
lessons.model: The adult pushes a bean bag from the neck (shot), then throws a light stick over the shoulder (javelin).
lessons.guided: Throw a bean bag with the shot movement and a light stick with the javelin movement. Measure with steps.
lessons.exercise: Where do others stand during throws?
lessons.remediation: Practise the movement without the object first.
lessons.transfer: Explain the safety rule to a younger child.
lessons.materials: Bean bags, light sticks or balls, open space.

practice.prompt: Match each event with its movement.
practice.answer: shot: push; javelin: over the shoulder; discus: turn.

practice.prompt: When do we collect the objects?
Tabi throws 6 steps, Ekane 8 steps. Who throws further?

lessons.title: Celebrating a birth in our culture
lessons.objective: Describe a significant life event of the community and draw lessons from it.
lessons.course:
Communities celebrate important events: the birth of a child (naming ceremony, visits, gifts), marriage (meeting of families, gifts, celebration), enthronement of a ruler.
Each event has customs, songs, dances and food. These events show solidarity and joy.
lessons.model: The adult tells how a recent birth was celebrated in the family: visitors, gifts, the choice of the name.
lessons.guided: Ask an elder how births are celebrated in your culture. Tell it in a few sentences, using some words of the family language.
lessons.answer: For example: a birth, a marriage or an enthronement.
lessons.remediation: Look at photos of a family event with an adult.
lessons.transfer: Ask your parents the meaning of your own name.

practice.prompt: Which event celebrates a new baby?
Write three sentences about a family celebration.
practice.explanation: Say what happened and how people felt.

practice.prompt: What do these events show?

lessons.title: Typing in Notepad: space bar, backspace, capital letters
lessons.objective: Use the keyboard to type letters and figures, with the space bar, backspace and capital letters.
lessons.course:
On the keyboard: the space bar puts a space between words; backspace deletes the letter on the left; Shift + a letter gives a capital letter; Caps Lock writes all in capitals; Enter goes to a new line.
Notepad is a simple program to type text.
lessons.model: The adult opens Notepad and types: “My name is Bih.” using Shift for M and B, and the space bar between words.
lessons.guided: With an adult, type your name and a sentence in Notepad. Correct a mistake with backspace. If there is no computer, practise on a paper keyboard.
lessons.exercise: Which key deletes the letter on the left?
lessons.remediation: Practise only the space bar and backspace first.
lessons.transfer: Type a short message to a family member with an adult.
lessons.materials: A computer with Notepad, or a paper keyboard.

practice.prompt: Match each key with its role.
practice.answer: space bar: space; Shift: capital; Enter: new line.

practice.prompt: How do we type a capital B?
Write the sentence you would type, with capitals and spaces.
practice.answer: A sentence with a capital letter and spaces.
